paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Round after round, Israel rebelled, in Egypt, in the wilderness, and in the land. Three times God resolved to pour out His wrath (Ezekiel 20:8, 13, 21), and three times He acted "for the sake of My name" (Ezekiel 20:9, 14, 22). Their record was a mess, but His name was never in question.

That's why the passage ends the way it does. God says He will deal with them "for the sake of My name and not according to your wicked ways and corrupt acts" (Ezekiel 20:44). He will gather them, accept them, and bring them into the land He swore to give their fathers (Ezekiel 20:41-42). Hear that, baker? The people who earned the least got the promise that stayed put.

Now, the same passage is NOT soft on sin. God refused to be consulted by the elders who came to inquire of the LORD (Ezekiel 20:1-3), and He says the rebels will not enter the land (Ezekiel 20:38). So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery: take sin seriously, and take God's mercy more seriously. I spent years in the back of a drawer feeling like my record said it all, and I'm telling you, it was never my record that got me out.
